integrity: The proof partitions codes by the membership of the two spine vertices. If one spine vertex is omitted, the solid trace-incomparability condition forces all opposite page vertices; if both are omitted, all page vertices are forced. If both spine vertices are selected, an entirely omitted page forces every other page to be full, while otherwise each page may independently contribute its left endpoint, right endpoint, or both. These four disjoint families are checked directly for sufficiency and counted exactly. A standalone exhaustive checker independently tests every vertex subset for m=1..8 and matches both the accepted family and every polynomial coefficient.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to square-page book graphs B_m with m at least one.
No formula is claimed for triangular books, longer-cycle books, or arbitrary generalized theta graphs.
The exhaustive computation covers m from one through eight and is corroborative only.
A differently named or non-indexed all-code enumeration may exist outside the retrieved literature.
title: Solid-locating-dominating code polynomial of square-page book graphs
